subject: Private CP operator onboarding and JIT access flow
messages:
From: Joe Miller <joe.miller@acme-corp.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: SaaS Infra <infra@acme-corp.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Jul 2028 09:12:34 -0700
Subject: Private CP: operator onboarding and JIT access flow questions

Hi Naomi —

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. Our SecOps team reviewed the Private Control Plane (VPC) operator model and we have a few concrete questions before we start SCIM/SAML work on our side: 

1) For operators created via SCIM, can Redwood emit ephemeral IAM role ARNs that map to short-lived certs on our side (we want JIT elevation for maintenance windows)?
2) What attributes do you expect in the SAML assertion for role mapping? We have about eight operator roles (operator-read, operator-write, operator-oncall, operator-admin) and need an attribute contract we can align to.
3) We're trying to avoid one-off shared service accounts. Is there a recommended pattern for operator service accounts vs. human SSO accounts for jumpbox access?

We're attaching our initial SCIM mapping spreadsheet and a sample SAML assertion we captured from our IdP. Can your team propose a minimal JIT flow that satisfies our audit controls (short TTL, MFA enforced at IdP, audit logs exported to our SIEM)?

Attachments: scim-operator-mapping-v1.xlsx, saml-assertion-example.txt

Best,
Joe Miller
Head of Platform Security
Acme Corp
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Joe Miller <joe.miller@acme-corp.com>
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Jul 2028 08:05:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Private CP: operator onboarding and JIT access flow questions

Joe —

Thanks for the clear list. Attached are a few notes from our side and an initial proposal sketch for a JIT+SCIM hybrid:

- SCIM provisioning: we consume groups mapped to "operator-*" roles. We create a stable operator identity in the Private CP and map it to a role binding. SCIM patch events drive creation/deprovisioning.
- JIT elevation: we recommend issuing short-lived operator credentials (12-60 minute TTL) from the private control plane via an API endpoint that validates an IdP SAML assertion + step-up MFA. Redwood will sign an ephemeral certificate that your jumpbox accepts for SSH or API mTLS.
- Assertion contract: include attributes: email, uid, groups (array), auth_time, acr (MFA level). For operator mapping we key on groups and a custom attribute operator_level=<read|write|oncall|admin>.
- Audit/logging: Redwood streams operator session events (start/stop, IP, action set) to an S3 endpoint or syslog collector. We can push to your SIEM via the same webhook used for audit exports.

Open questions for us: how strict is Acme on TTL (we can tune) and do you require cross-account role ARNs (AWS) or a cert approach? Both are possible — certs are easier for on-prem jumpboxes.

I'll loop in Priyom and Ben to propose a concrete config and a sample SCIM schema change.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Security PM — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Joe Miller <joe.miller@acme-corp.com>
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 10:34:50 -0700
Subject: Re: Private CP: operator onboarding and JIT access flow questions

Quick technical draft from our infra side — marking up the attributes and a small diagram (attached). Bottom line: cert-based JIT is our recommended default for on-prem jumpboxes; cross-account ARNs for cloud-native operator automation.

Implementation notes: 
- SCIM: canonical attributes (userName, externalId, displayName, groups, entitlements). We'll add operator_level as an extension: urn:redwood:operator_level.
- SAML assertion mapping: map groups -> operator role. If operator_level exists, it overrides group mapping. Example assertion snippet in saml-assertion-example.txt.
- Ephemeral cert flow:
  * User authenticates with IdP and completes MFA (IdP emits assertion with auth_time and acr).
  * Acme's connector calls Redwood's /v1/privcp/jit/request with assertion.
  * Redwood validates assertion against configured IdP metadata, checks group/attribute contract, and issues a signed cert (PEM) valid for requested lifetime (bounded by an account-level max TTL).
  * The cert and event are logged; a webhook event is emitted to Acme SIEM.

Security controls: support for eKYC or manual approval step (can be toggled). TTL defaults: 15 minutes for operator-oncall, 60 minutes max for operator-admin (configurable).

Attachments: operator-oncall-jit-diagram.png

I'll prepare a short runbook and a sample SCIM patch payload for Priyom to review.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Infra Engineer, Private Inference
Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Joe Miller <joe.miller@acme-corp.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 29 Jul 2028 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private CP: operator onboarding and JIT access flow questions

Joe —

We iterated on the config and Priyom validated compatibility with our SCIM connector. Summary of agreed plan and next steps: 

1) Attribute contract (final): userName, email, groups, urn:redwood:operator_level, externalId, auth_time, acr.
2) Provisioning cadence: SCIM delta provisioning, immediate deprovision on delete event.
3) JIT flow (cert-based) for on-prem jumpbox access: default TTL 15m for oncall, 60m max for admin. Redwood will sign certs; Acme will trust Redwood CA for operator certs.
4) Audit & export: webhook to Acme SIEM (HMAC signed), and 90-day event retention in Private CP by default (configurable).
5) Optional manual approval: Acme can enable an approval workflow (Slack/Email webhook) for admin-level elevation.

Deliverables we will provide this sprint (ETA 2 weeks):
- SCIM patch examples and sample mapping (scim-operator-mapping-v1.xlsx)
- SAML attribute/metadata file and validation checklist (saml-assertion-example.txt)
- JIT runbook + operational playbook for oncall rotations (will include rollover steps for emergency access)

Can we schedule a 30-minute handoff next Monday (Aug 6) for the runbook review and a short test plan? If that works I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — appreciate the quick back-and-forth.

Naomi Feldman
Senior Security PM — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
